prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "proof", with the standing line "Holds each extracted page against a picture of the original, mending only the scanner's mistakes and leaving the author's words alone." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows At left, a stack of typed pages from extracted.md, each topped by a page N marker; one page slides out. Beside it, the book.pdf lies open; the matching page passes through pdftoppm and becomes a crisp page image. The typed page and the page image lie side by side on one reading desk beneath a vision model that reads both at once. Small marks in the typed text are corrected against the image. The mended page moves right and rejoins the stack, which carries on rightward toward the output. All arrows run left to right: text and PDF in, mended text out.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one, the long-s ſ read as f and corrected to s. Circle two, a word split at a line end rejoined into one word. Circle three, colour and connexion untouched despite old spelling. study one, a nearly empty page under 40 characters passing straight through. Study two, a page whose image failed to render, original kept. Study three, a page whose model call errored, original kept. Study four, a start page and end page bracket around a run of pages.

Colour is used so that : Vermilion marks every correction the model makes. Ochre marks every uncertain flag left for a human. Slate grey marks pages passed through untouched.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: S: 2 inputs, extracted text and PDF, converging on 1 output. 1 page image per page, rendered at 200 DPI. Pages under 40 characters skipped. 3 pass-through cases: short page, render failure, API error. 2 spend tiers: cheap and pro.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: Y: extracted.md on the input stack; book.pdf on the open book; page N on each page marker; pdftoppm on the renderer; page image on the rendered picture; vision model on the reader above the desk; long-s ſ in the first circle; uncertain: old → new on the ochre flag; proofed.md on the finished stack; cost ledger beside the total; cheap or pro on the model; start page and end page on the bracket; dry run on the empty desk study.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: : extracted.md, book.pdf, page N, pdftoppm, 200 DPI, page image, extracted text, vision model, mended text, cheap or pro. long-s ſ, misread as f, broken ligature, rejoined word, colour stays, connexion stays. under 40 characters, render failed, API error, original kept, start page, end page, dry run. proofed.md, uncertain: old → new, cost ledger, total cost. fix scanning damage, keep author's words, confess uncertainty.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: S: The page image is the authority; One page at a time. Spelling, grammar, punctuation, capitals all stand. Skipped pages pass through, with a warning; Dry run lists pages, spends nothing. Doubtful fixes wait for a human judge; Every call recorded, total printed. Anthropic or OpenAI models only.
